articles.title: Tom Skerritt obituary
articles.summary: US actor who often played authority figures and was admired for his film roles in Alien, Top Gun and A River Runs Through It. The lean, rugged US actor Tom Skerritt, who has died aged 93, was described by one screenwriter as “a character actor trapped in a leading man’s body”.
body: Skerritt’s breakthrough had come in the 1970 film M*A*S*H, directed by Robert Altman. He played Augustus “Duke” Forrest, a US army surgeon in the Korean war exuding southern charm at the 4077th Mobile Army Surgical Hospital. Along with his fellow surgeons, Benjamin Franklin “Hawkeye” Pierce ( played by Donald Sutherland ) and “Trapper” John McIntyre (Elliott Gould), Duke displayed cynicism and irreverence towards his superiors.

But Skerritt’s character was not transferred to the TV series that followed. While some sources reported that the actor had no faith in the film working as a half-hour sitcom, the writer Larry Gelbart, who adapted the novel for the small screen with Gene Reynolds, explained they wanted characters they felt could generate storylines, adding: “Trapper John just seemed more colourful than Duke.”

Skerritt remained prolific in character roles in films and on TV until coming to worldwide attention as the doomed Captain Dallas, in charge of the commercial space tug Nostromo, in the sci-fi horror movie Alien (1979), which made a star of Sigourney Weaver.

articles.title: Acrobatic Pastor’s Secret Obsession Drives Boo Junfeng’s ‘Trinity’ at Tokyo Gap-Financing Market
articles.summary: A celebrity preacher who performs daredevil stunts for his congregation while hiding his fixation on a young follower sits at the center of “Trinity,” the new feature from director Boo Junfeng, which is among the projects at this year’s Tokyo Gap-Financing Market.
body: Though publicly known for his conservative stance, Johnny grows infatuated with Yang, a newcomer to his training program, and his preferential treatment of the young man soon becomes hard to miss. It unsettles his wife Ruth, and David, his leading disciple and his daughter’s husband-to-be, both of whom share in running the church.

When Yang vanishes, a frantic Johnny starts his own inquiry. The clues point toward the people in his inner circle, with tragic results. Johnny and Ruth later relocate to rural Taiwan, where they keep a low profile and worship at a modest local congregation – until Johnny glimpses an enigmatic stranger who may yet bring the couple divine grace.
“I’ve always been very interested in the subject of sexuality and faith, and I wanted to make a film that dives deep into the psyche of these characters within a church,” Boo said.

articles.title: ‘The One About Matthew Perry’ Director on Gaining His Sister’s Trust, Explaining How He Died and More
articles.summary: SPOILER ALERT: This post contains conversation about all three episodes of “The One About Matthew Perry,” now streaming on Netflix. At the end of Netflix’s new docuseries “The One About Matthew Perry,” director Mary Robertson can be heard saying something off camera.
body: Robertson is the first to say she doesn’t believe in things she can’t see. But having spent months with the memories of Perry told through his loved ones, she admitted to one of the people who knew him best that he was more than just stories to her after this process.

Bowick has never spoken openly about her brother’s decadeslong struggle with addiction, but now shares the full scope of Perry’s life from inside the family, including their relationship as half siblings who share the same father, actor John Bennett Perry. The series charts Perry’s meteoric rise from being a working actor to a global comedic star, thanks to “Friends” and his character Chandler Bing, and what ultimately becomes the biggest role of his life –– an advocate for addiction rehabilitation while continuously suffering from the disease himself.

She also gives new details about private moments, including repeated visits to see him in rehab and being at his bedside in 2018 after his near-fatal colon rupture. “This is it, he is not waking up,” Bowick says in Episode 3, recalling her reaction when she first arrived at the hospital.

articles.title: Japanese Producers Drive Tokyo Market Growth as Exhibition Space Sells Out
articles.summary: The Tokyo International Film Festival’s TIFFCOM market exhibition space sold out early this year, according to managing director Ikeda Kaori. More Japanese producers are using the Tokyo market to find partners while projects are still in development.
body: “Beyond the traditional trading of completed content, TIFFCOM has increasingly evolved into a platform for finding partners from the project development stage, leading to a significant increase in participation by Japanese producers,” Ikeda tells Variety.
She also points to Asia, which is now one of the world’s largest markets. Governments across the region are actively backing their content industries, she says.

This year’s Tokyo IP Market has grown to 10 participating IP holders and adds new categories, toys among them. The pitch event has also changed format. Each company now gives a focused pitch on its flagship IP.

The changes come after the market’s expansion to the Cannes Film Market this year, where more than 700 people registered for its pitches, panels and related programs. The audience was mostly from Europe and Hollywood. Ikeda says the IP holders who took part held a run of meetings with partners they rarely get to see in person. An initiative proposed by the Cannes market also set up matchmaking with the XR sector.

articles.title: ‘Altadena: One Fire After Another’ Documentary Set by Former ’60 Minutes’ Producers (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Climate journalist Bill McKibben and executive producer and former “60 Minutes” producer David Gelber have teamed up to create “Altadena: One Fire After Another,” a documentary chronicling the aftermath of the 2025 Eaton Fire in Los Angeles.
body: “The fire was only the beginning of the story,” Gelber said in a statement. “We wanted to understand what happens after the television cameras leave, when families are left to rebuild not only their homes but also their lives and sense of community. Altadena’s story is deeply personal, but it’s also a window into questions communities across the country are increasingly facing.”
The film features interviews with Altadena residents sharing personal stories along with conversations with professionals on climate, economics and public policy.

“We’ve become accustomed to covering disasters as breaking news. What’s far less visible is what comes next. This film is about the months and years after a catastrophe, when the real consequences begin to unfold,” McKibben said in a statement. “I hope people take away from the documentary the fact that this is not a random tragedy in any way; rather, it’s caused by a particular set of players doing a particular thing.”

articles.title: ‘How on earth is this man not sweating?’ Director Brett Morgen’s painstaking 10-year remaser Bowie’s ‘greatest filmed performance’
articles.summary: Moonage Daydream director Brett Morgan has turned lost footage of two 1978 concerts into an arena spectacular. ‘You can feel the danger and excitement’, he says. • ‘Lost’ 1978 David Bowie tour film to play arenas in 2027, remastered by Moonage Daydream director Brett Morgen.
body: I n 2017, when Brett Morgen began work on his acclaimed 2022 David Bowie documentary, Moonage Daydream, he was given complete access to the late star’s entire, cavernous archive. “My eyes were immediately drawn to a stack of gleaming 35mm cans with the word ‘Stage’ written on them,” he remembers.

At first, the director – whose work also includes Kurt Cobain: Montage of Heck and the Rolling Stones documentary Crossfire Hurricane – assumed the cans might contain some sort of footage shot around Bowie’s 1978 live album, Stage, recorded in mostly in Philadelphia. However, he soon realised they actually contained the holy grail of Bowie artefacts: footage of the legendary Earl’s Court shows later that year, which had remained unseen for almost 50 years. “Making Moonage Daydream, I had access to every filmed performance in existence of David Bowie,” he says, “but when I saw this one I knew this was without question the greatest filmed performance of his career.”

articles.title: Elon Musk’s AI Odyssey review – the dullest, most pointless riposte possible to Christopher Nolan’s brilliant epic
articles.summary: It is hardly a shock that Grok AI’s interpretation of Homer is as meaningless as a laptop screensaver. The only surprise would be if Musk accepted defeat graciously. Which he won’t. Think back.
body: Think back. Do you remember when Elon Musk, in a weird online tantrum, and without having seen the film, condemned the supposed wokery in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, for getting Elliot Page to play Sinon and Lupita Nyong’o to play Helen of Troy? As the plaudits and the box-office receipts for Nolan’s Odyssey piled stratospherically up, Musk showed that being a good loser is not among his qualities. He petulantly exclaimed that he could do his own better and more authentic Odyssey on Grok AI. And now he has released the first online seven-minute “episode” to a world that has long since forgotten about this claim and didn’t care in the first place.

articles.title: Adventurer completes 400-mile expedition after losing contact with team
articles.summary: Ash Dykes is trying to complete six back-to-back expeditions in a variety of extreme environments.
body: An adventurer has completed the first leg of his latest challenge after losing contact with his UK team for almost 24 hours.
Ash Dykes, 35, from Old Colwyn, Conwy, holds five world records but his most recent quest was the first of six back-to-back expeditions he will take on in extreme environments.
Dykes encountered elephants, gorillas and was chased by "killer" bees as he rowed more than 434 miles (700 km) along rivers in the Congo Basin, central Africa.
Towards the end of the journey, Dykes' portable satellite kit lost power. He said: "My parents and fiancée were worrying but as soon as I had a bit of signal I made sure I got in touch".

articles.title: Arnie & Barney review – dimwit ant double-act from Maya the Bee are on mission to entertain
articles.summary: From the ugly design to the lacklustre script, this is one parents might want to skip this half-term holiday. In 1912 in Germany, antisemitic writer Waldemar Bonsels published The Adventures of Maya the Bee, which later became a 1970s anime series in Japan called Maya the Honey Bee, and was later…
body: The film opens very much in media res, with a young female bee flying through outer space clutching a small pig and droplet of water the size of her head. She’s being pursued aggressively by a handful of wasp-type creatures and a narrator solemnly intones: “Sometimes the most unlikely heroes … become legends.” The bee then stops next to a couple of red ants and asks what they’re doing. They are the narrators, they explain, but this his is all soon revealed as fantasy – the pair of ants are telling a story to a larger platoon of ants. Some exposition follows about the ants’ mission: to find fresh water.

This is fine as far as it goes, perhaps, but what a précis can’t convey is quite how staggeringly ugly and uninteresting the whole endeavour is. It starts with the character design: it’s hard to imagine any but the most aesthetically starved children embracing this ant pair. Boy are they a chore to spend time with, both visually and in terms of the lacklustre script. Even if you are struggling for entertainment options you might want to do the kids a favour and skip this one.

articles.title: Unnamed celebrity accused of 'inappropriate sexual activities', court hears
articles.summary: The man is asking the High Court to prevent two news organisations from publishing the allegations.
body: A celebrity has asked the High Court to prevent two news organisations from publishing his identity and allegations that he abused his status for many years to engage, or attempt to engage, in "inappropriate sexual activities with a large number of girls and young women".
The unnamed celebrity is seeking an injunction, and his legal team told the first day of a trial on Tuesday that any publication would be "highly likely" to lead him to kill himself.
They told the court that his drastic reaction was not because of any wrongdoing, but because of the fear of "trial by media".
The man denies abusing "his power and position as a celebrity to contact and forge relationships with young women and teenagers to try to have sex with them", the court heard.
